scope: test architecture, inventory, governance, registry prototype and CI only; no production or qualified-reference changes

items.assessment: One-kernel architecture is indexed, not forked into use-case-specific kernels.
Testbank I/O and orchestration remain outside the computational kernel.
Registry distinguishes parameters, state, forcing, numerical configuration and results.
No persistent column state is added; registry metadata is external.
No worker scratch ownership is changed.
No storage-layout constraint is introduced; MultiSWAP scale remains an explicit qualification axis.
Checkpoint, trial/retry, commit and rollback are a required TB-L4 contract.
Replay and warm-start qualification are supported without changing committed physical-state authority.
Cases use generic [t0,t1]; calendar assumptions are not introduced.
Coupling cases are defined for generic windows rather than day boundaries.
Coupling is a first-class TB-L8 qualification layer.
Head and flux interface contract is explicit; flux conservation is hard and head tolerance application-bound.
Hard mass gate is horizontal and cannot be waived by execution profile.
Interface sensitivities and response tangents are explicit solver/coupling qualification targets.
Coupling cost is separated from scientific correctness and retained as a qualification target.
MultiSWAP is a primary TB-L9/TB-L10 axis including large-scale future cases.
Tile aggregation and non-1:1 groundwater mapping remain coupler/runtime concerns.
Deep-vadose transfer is treated as an optional external coupling component.
Transition between transfer-zone and direct coupling is required to conserve stored water.
Alternative soil-water solvers are first-class TB-L3 targets behind a common interface.
Shared process physics is qualified across solver variants rather than duplicated.
Hydraulic information is tested through contracts, not HeadCalc internals.
Physical switches and solver/numerical policy are separate registry dimensions.
Bounded-cost and difficult-column qualification cannot override mass or science gates.
Full/reference mode remains an explicit oracle/reference route.
Diagnostics, retries, fallbacks, solver cost and mass residuals are report fields.
Optional functionality and inactive-option cost/state are explicit coverage targets.
System composition relationships remain outside the SWAP kernel.
Registry and architecture add no hidden midnight, daily, file-format or direct-MODFLOW assumptions.
This audit explicitly assesses all architecture invariants for the F-TB01 change.
